transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. 

Um, I guess what made me bring it up and come in today is that... well, for the past few weeks, my eating has just been a little off. I hope it's okay to start with that. I've been finding myself skipping breakfast and lunch without really meaning to. It's not on purpose or anything. And then I end up just picking at dinner, even when my wife cooked, which I feel terrible about because I really don't want her to think I'm ungrateful or being difficult. 

But, um, I noticed my jeans are starting to feel kind of loose lately. Is... is that the sort of thing I should be telling you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

Oh, no, definitely not. Um... I really haven't been trying to. I know it probably sounds a little irresponsible of me to just be dropping weight like that, and I promise I'm not trying to be unhealthy or anything. It's just... the drive to eat just hasn't really been there. 

I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm doing this on purpose, or like I'm neglecting myself intentionally. I really am trying my best to keep up with things.
Are you worried about your weight loss?

Um... no, not really worried, I guess? I mean, I hope it's okay to say that. I just figured it wasn't a huge amount of weight or anything to panic over, so I haven't really been stressing about it. 

But... should I be worried? I really don't want to brush it off if you think it's a serious problem. If you want me to start weighing myself or keeping a closer eye on it, I definitely can do that. I just want to make sure I'm doing whatever I'm supposed to be doing.
Have you noticed any changes in your interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Um... no, I don't think so. I've still been doing my usual stuff. I mean, I still try to keep busy with the things I like. I hope that's okay? 

I just... I haven't really lost interest in anything, as far as I can tell. I'm sorry if that's not the answer you were looking for, or if it doesn't help figure things out. I really do try to stay engaged with my hobbies so I'm not just sitting around being unproductive. Is... is that normal?
Are you afraid of gaining weight?

Um... no, not at all, actually. I mean, I hope that doesn't make the weight loss seem even more confusing. I promise I don't have any, like, fear of putting the weight back on or anything like that. 

If you think I need to gain some of it back to be healthy, I am completely on board with trying to do that. I really just want to do whatever you think is best for my health. Does... does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Are you afraid of eating?

Um... no, definitely not. I'm not afraid of eating at all. I hope it doesn't seem like I'm doing this on purpose. I still eat when I'm hungry, I promise. 

I just... I don't know, maybe I haven't been as hungry lately? But I'm not scared of food or anything. If you want me to try eating more or keep a food diary, I can totally do that. I just want to make sure I'm doing the right thing. Is that... does that help?
Do you feel like you have less appetite than you used to?

Um... yeah, I guess maybe a little bit. I hope it's not a big deal, but... for the past few weeks, my eating has just been kind of off. Like, I'll end up skipping breakfast and lunch without really meaning to. And then at dinner, I kind of just pick at my food... even when my wife cooks. Which I feel terrible about, because she's a great cook, I promise! I just haven't had the appetite for it. 

And, um, I guess my jeans are starting to feel a little loose because of it. I'm really trying to do better, though, and eat more when she makes dinner. Does... does that make sense? I hope that helps explain the weight thing.
Do you feel upset or anxious about your eating habits?

Um... no, not really upset or anxious, I don't think. I mean, I feel bad about my wife's cooking, like I said, but... I'm not stressing out about the food itself or anything. I just kind of noticed it recently. 

I'm really not trying to cause any trouble with it, I promise. I know it's important to eat right. If you think I should be paying closer attention to it, I absolutely will. I just want to be a good patient and do what you think is best. Is... is it okay that I'm not anxious about it?
Do you think your lack of appetite is related to anything going on in your life or your thoughts?

Um... I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't really noticed any specific thoughts or, you know, big life events that would make me stop wanting to eat. I mean, things have been pretty normal, I think? 

I hope that's not a bad answer. I'm really trying to think if there's something I'm missing, but... it just kind of happened, I guess? I really don't want to make it seem like I'm hiding anything from you, I promise. I just... I don't know what's causing it. Is that... is it normal to just not know why?
How much weight would you say you've lost over the past few weeks?

Um... I haven't actually weighed myself, to be honest. I didn't want to make a big deal out of it, you know? It's probably just a couple of pounds... nothing crazy, I promise. Just enough to make my jeans a tiny bit loose, like I mentioned. 

I mean, I don't look sickly or anything, right? I really hope I don't. I'm sure it's not a lot of weight. If you want me to start weighing myself, I can definitely do that. Whatever you think is best.
Has your lack of appetite been consistent over the past few weeks?

Um... yeah, I think it's been pretty consistent, mostly. I mean, I haven't really had any days where I suddenly felt super hungry or anything. It's just been this steady... lack of interest in eating, I guess. 

I really hope that's the right kind of answer. I'm not trying to be difficult or vague, I just haven't been keeping a super close eye on it every single day. But it feels like it's been pretty much the same the whole time. Is that... does that make sense for what you usually see?
Have you noticed any decrease in enjoyment of your hobbies or other activities you normally like to do?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I still try to do the things I usually enjoy, like reading or watching a movie. I haven't completely stopped doing them or anything. 

I guess maybe I'm a little less focused on them right now, but I still like them. I really don't want you to think I'm just sitting around doing nothing all day. I'm trying to keep up with my normal routine, I promise. It's just... maybe I get tired a little faster? But I still enjoy my hobbies. That's a good sign, right?
Would you say the weight loss has been significant enough that others have noticed?

Um... well, my wife actually did say something the other day. That's kind of what made me bring it up in the first place, actually. She noticed I've been skipping breakfast and lunch without really meaning to, and then I just sort of pick at dinner, even when she cooks something I usually like. 

She's the one who pointed out that my jeans are starting to look a little loose on me. I really didn't want her to worry, so I tried to eat a bit more, but it's just hard right now. I hope she's not too upset with me about it. But yeah, I guess someone else did notice. Is it... is it bad that she noticed? I'm trying to do better, I really am.
Have you been feeling sad or depressed lately?

Um... well, I wouldn't say I'm like, crying all the time or anything dramatic like that. I'm really trying to keep a good attitude. But... yeah, I guess I've been feeling a bit down. 

Most days lately, I just wake up with this... heavy, flat feeling. It's like the apartment is just too quiet, you know? And even when I try to do things to cheer myself up, like picking up my guitar, it just doesn't really lift me the way it usually does. 

I'm sorry, I know that sounds a little gloomy. I don't want to sound like I'm just complaining. I'm really trying to shake it off, I promise. It's just... it's been a little tough to feel like my normal self. Is that... is that pretty common for people to feel like that sometimes?
Are you afraid of being fat?

Oh... no, no, not at all. I mean, I know I just said I've been losing a little weight and skipping meals, but it's definitely not because I'm worried about my size or anything like that. I'm really not trying to diet or restrict myself. 

I actually want to stay healthy, I promise. It's just... the appetite just isn't really there right now. But I'm definitely not afraid of gaining weight. I hope you don't think I'm doing this on purpose? Because I really am trying to eat when I can, I know it's important to keep my strength up. That's the right thing to do, isn't it?
Do you find that your lack of appetite is worse at certain times of the day?

Um... I haven't really noticed it being worse at any specific time, honestly. I think it's just kind of... generally low all day. 

Like I said, I usually end up skipping breakfast and lunch, but it's not like I feel more hungry or less hungry then, I just sort of... forget to eat, I guess? And by dinner, I try to make an effort, especially since my wife goes to the trouble of cooking, but I still just don't have much of an urge to eat. 

So I wouldn't say there's a certain time that's worse. It's just a mild thing throughout the day. I am trying to pay more attention to it, though, and eat more regularly. That's probably what I should be doing, right? Just trying to stick to a schedule even if I'm not super hungry?
Do you think your lack of appetite is related to your feeling down or sad?

Um... I guess I haven't really put two and two together, honestly. I suppose they could be connected? I mean, when you say it like that, it does make sense. 

But I really try hard not to let feeling a little down affect my daily habits, you know? I don't want to be someone who just stops taking care of themselves just because they're in a bit of a funk. I'm really trying to keep pushing forward. 

So I haven't exactly noticed a direct link myself, but... maybe you're right and they are tied together. Is that pretty typical for people? Like, if I can just work on getting my mood back up and staying positive, my appetite will probably just naturally follow, right? I'd like to think I can get back on track if I just try a little harder.
Do you think your lack of appetite started around the same time as you began feeling down?

Gosh, um... I really wish I had a better answer for you. I honestly didn't keep track of the exact timeline. 

I mean, maybe? It's possible they sort of... drifted in around the same time. But I really try not to dwell on it when I'm feeling a little off, you know? I just try to keep a smile on and push through it, so I might have just completely missed the early signs. 

I hope it's alright that I don't know for sure. I'm really trying to be as helpful as I can with your questions. Do most people usually remember exactly when these things start? I should probably be paying closer attention to myself, shouldn't I?
Do you think your lack of appetite would improve if your mood lifted?

Um... I would really like to think so. I guess I don't know for absolute sure, just because I haven't really... well, I haven't experienced it yet, I suppose. 

But it makes a lot of sense when you put it that way. I'd like to imagine that if I can just get back to my normal self and stay positive, my appetite will just sort of fix itself. I really hope that's how it works, anyway. I'd hate for this to be a permanent thing. 

Is that usually what happens when people start feeling better? I just really want to make sure I'm doing whatever I can to get back on track and be a good patient for you.
Do you think your appetite would return to normal if you weren't feeling down?

Um, yeah... I think, like I was trying to say just a second ago, I really, really hope it would. I'm sorry, did I not explain that very well the first time? I know I tend to ramble a bit when I'm trying to figure things out, so I apologize if I was being confusing. 

I honestly don't know for an absolute fact, just because I'm still trying to pull myself out of this little slump. But I'd imagine if I wasn't feeling down anymore, my body would just sort of bounce back and I'd be eating normally again. I'm really trying my best not to let it get out of hand in the meantime, though. 

I hope I'm giving you the right answers here... I just want to make sure I'm being clear and giving you what you need to help me. Does that make sense?
